name: Investor Incentive and Decision-Process Alignment

positioning.oneLineSummary: Maps who actually decides, what each capital provider optimizes, and where future financing or strategic conflicts may arise.
positioning.productLabel: Investor Alignment Lens — based on Scott Kupor public materials
notAClaimOf: financial investors always being superior to strategic investors
an investor commitment beyond signed documents

attribution.display: Based on Scott Kupor and Frank Chen's public investor-selection episode

neutralParaphrase: Capital providers can differ in return objective, strategic objective, time horizon, decision authority, governance rights, reserve capacity, and follow-on behavior. Before relying on an investor, identify the actual decision-makers and signed rights. Brand, partner title, or prior behavior at another fund is not sufficient.

locator.value: Official episode scope: LP/GP incentives, economic and governance interests, corporate VC, and firm decision process

requiredConditions: At least one external capital provider may receive economic or governance rights.
Investor identity, fund vehicle, and responsible partner can be resolved.
Future financing or strategic optionality matters.

requiredEvidence.description: Exact legal investor entity, fund vintage, mandate, decision body, responsible partner, and conflicts.
Signed economic, governance, information, transfer, pro-rata, and veto rights.
Reserve policy, fund age, concentration limits, and stated participation expectations.
Customer, partner, competitor, acquisition, data, and exclusivity conflicts created by the investor.

decisionQuestions: Who can approve, block, or delay this investment?
What does each investor optimize: financial return, strategic access, option value, or another objective?
Which promises are contractual and which are relational?
What future round participation is realistic for this vehicle?
Could the investor constrain customers, partners, acquirers, or later investors?
How will conflicts be surfaced and resolved?
positiveSignals: Decision authority and timeline are explicit.
Economic and strategic objectives are disclosed and compatible.
Follow-on expectations match fund capacity and are documented.
Potential commercial conflicts have workable safeguards.
Founder and investor can describe difficult-scenario incentives consistently.
redFlags: The team relies on a brand without knowing the approving body.
A strategic investor creates exclusivity or signalling risk.
A partner promises follow-on without reserve authority.
Governance rights materially exceed the investor's stated role.
Different stakeholders describe the same commitment differently.
disconfirmingEvidence: The actual fund is late in life or reserve-constrained.
Historical follow-on behavior contradicts stated expectations.
Strategic conflicts block customers, partners, or acquirers.
The responsible partner lacks internal sponsorship or authority.
Signed documents allocate materially different rights than the relationship narrative.
contraindications: Do not infer alignment from firm brand or partner title.
Do not treat verbal support as committed capital.
Do not use prior portfolio outcomes as proof of future support.

instructions: Resolve the exact investor entity and decision authority.
Separate economic, governance, strategic, and relational incentives.
Map signed rights and unstated expectations.
Test downside, follow-on, acquisition, and conflict scenarios.
Return an alignment map and unresolved commitments.

sourceReliability.low: Investor incentives are described only by third parties.
sourceReliability.medium: Official episode scope and direct confirmations are available.
sourceReliability.high: First-party timestamps, signed documents, and fund-specific evidence converge.

evidenceStrength.medium: Decision process and some rights are confirmed.
evidenceStrength.high: Entity, authority, rights, reserves, conflicts, and scenarios are documented.

evidenceCoverage.low: Decision authority or rights are missing.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Current round is covered but future scenarios are incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: Current, follow-on, downside, strategic, and exit incentives are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: No external investor rights or dependency exist.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: Alignment matters but investor details remain provisional.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Investor choice materially affects financing or strategic optionality.

judgmentConfidence.low: The conclusion relies on relationship impressions.
judgmentConfidence.medium: Most incentives are clear with unresolved future commitments.

promotionRequirements: Pin investor and board video timestamps.
Validate disclosed capacity and decision process against observed outcomes.
Separate legal rights from relationship quality.
empiricalQualifications: Investor incentives vary by vehicle, partner, and time.
Historical behavior may not transfer to a new fund or strategy.
Strategic conflicts can be company- and market-specific.

rights.notes: Official episode topics are paraphrased; no transcript mirror is used as a runtime source.

openIssues: Reconcile with Venture Deals and fund-governance frameworks.
